chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq, from 'Ammar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who has four wives, and one of them dies; is it permissible for him to marry another in her place? He said: 'No, until four months and ten days have passed for her.'
He was asked: And if he divorces one, is it permissible for him to marry? He said: 'No, until the waiting period of the divorced woman has passed for her.'
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is based on a type of preference (istihbab), because when the wife dies, it is permissible for the man to marry another woman in her place immediately.

key_terms.الاسْتِحْبَاب: Preference/Recommendation (a legal status between obligation and permissibility)
key_terms.عِدَّةُ الْمُطَلَّقَةِ: Waiting period of the divorced woman

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a man to marry a new wife to replace a deceased or divorced wife in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the ruling for a man with four wives wishing to replace a deceased or divorced spouse, specifying a waiting period of four months and ten days for the deceased and the full 'iddah for the divorced. Shaykh al-Tusi notes that Imam al-Sadiq’s answer is based on istihbab (preference) rather than strict prohibition (karahah), as immediate replacement is technically permissible. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly approach of distinguishing between legal validity and recommended practice in marital matters.
